jobs.description:
Discover your full potential. At Tetra Tech, we are collaborating with industry-leading experts for a sustainable future for our world. We combine consulting and engineering with advanced analytics and technology to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our innovation hubs across the globe will enable you to share ideas and best practices while growing your professional network. Wherever you are in your career journey, you will benefit from working with world-class engineers, scientists, and technical specialists.

At Tetra Tech, we are Leading with Science to solve the world’s most complex challenges. Our industry-leading experts in engineering and consulting are committed to driving positive change in communities around the world. For over 50 years, we have been at the forefront of innovation and sustainability. Today we stand as a market leader, offering cutting-edge solutions in water, environment, energy, and international development. Our work has improved more than 625 million lives around the world.

Join Tetra Tech to make a real difference. Our work leverages cutting-edge technologies, advanced analytics, and the expertise of world-class scientists and engineers to create meaningful change around the world. Discover your full potential – join us to advance your career while leaving a lasting legacy.

Apply today and join the company that is Leading with Science®.

Tetra Tech is seeking a self-motivated, Entry-Level Environmental Scientist / Compliance Specialist to support and expand our landfill and air quality compliance services within the solid waste industry. This position is ideal for candidates with a strong interest in air regulations, landfill gas systems, emissions compliance, and environmental data analysis.

In this role, you will support regulatory compliance programs by analyzing field and operational data, interpreting air quality regulations and permit requirements, preparing compliance reports, and assisting with air permitting and emissions calculations. The primary focus areas include landfill gas monitoring, Surface Emissions Monitoring (SEM), Landfill Gas-to-Energy (LFGTE) Systems, air quality permitting, and compliance with New Source Performance Standards (NSPS) and National Emissions Standards for Hazardous Pollutants (NESHAP) regulations applicable to solid waste facilities.

This position is primarily remote, with limited, as-needed travel or occasional site visits. Only those in PST or MST will be considered.
Candidates must be comfortable working independently with limited supervision while collaborating with project managers, field staff, engineers, and regulatory specialists across geographically dispersed teams.

This position is eligible for our full benefits package including but not limited to Medical, Dental, Vision, Life, AD&D, Disability, Flexible Spending Account (FSA), Health Spending Account (HSA), My Flex Time (MFT - paid time off), 401K, and an Employee Stock Purchase Plan. The pay range for this position is $55K-$75K annually, based on qualifications, location, and experience. Only those that attach a cover letter will be considered.
The deadline to apply is 09/3/2026.

Your Role

Review, analyze, and interpret landfill air quality and landfill gas monitoring data, including wellfield data, SEM, and air emissions datasets.
Compare monitoring and operational data against regulatory standards, permit limits, and NSPS/NESHAP criteria to assess compliance.
Prepare environmental compliance reports, including air compliance summaries, monitoring reports, deviation analyses, and regulatory submittals.
Support the development and preparation of air quality permit applications, amendments, and renewals, including emission calculations and regulatory compliance demonstrations.
Collect, manage, track, and organize large datasets related to air emissions, landfill gas, SEM results, and compliance deadlines.
Develop and maintain templates, trackers, and tools to support consistent, accurate, and timely reporting for multiple facilities / landfills.
Coordinate with on-site operations, technicians, and subcontractors to confirm that monitoring, testing, and system performance meet regulatory and permit requirements.
Support Project Managers with deliverables, schedules, and client coordination including procurement of supplies, subcontractor coordination and Work Order development.
Contribute to multidisciplinary teams on engineering, permitting, and environmental projects.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering, or a related field.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, including technical and regulatory writing.
Proficiency in MS Office – specifically Word and Excel.
Ability to work independently in a remote environment, demonstrate initiative, and manage multiple priorities with limited supervision.
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate effectively with field staff, engineers, and regulatory agencies.
Valid driver’s license.
Ability and willingness to perform limited travel as required.
Interest and ability in developing technical and leadership skills within the Environmental Compliance field.

Life At Tetra Tech

The perks of working at Tetra Tech include:

Comprehensive and market-competitive benefits.
Merit-based financial rewards.
Flexibility and company-wide commitment to work/life balance.
Collaborative team atmosphere that values the contributions of all employees.
Learning and development opportunities for ongoing professional growth.

About Tetra Tech

Tetra Tech is the leader in water, environment, and sustainable infrastructure, providing high-end consulting and engineering services for projects worldwide. With 25,000 employees working together, Tetra Tech provides clear solutions to complex problems by Leading with Science® to address the entire water cycle, protect and restore the environment, design sustainable and resilient infrastructure, and support the clean energy transition.

Tetra Tech
is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified candidates will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, age, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a protected veteran, or any other characteristic protected by law. Tetra Tech is a VEVRAA federal contractor and we request priority referral of veterans.

We thank all applicants for their interest, however, only those candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.

Please no phone calls or agencies.

jobs.description:
About Us

At Onterris, we build careers grounded in purpose, responsibility and real-world impact.

“For Planet and Progress” is our north star that guides everything we do. We believe environmental responsibility and human progress are interconnected, interwoven and international. Our scientists, engineers, field teams, consultants and professionals collaborate across disciplines and geographies, guiding industries and governments, ensuring that communities and environments thrive.

When you join us, you’re not just forging a career, you’re joining a movement. A movement for better thinking, smarter solutions and lasting impact.

Together, we will advance our way of life and protect the integrity of our environment every step of the way.

A Day in the Life

As an LDAR Field Technician, you’ll be responsible for performing inspections on various types of facilities in the Oil and Gas Industry to identify and quantify hydrocarbon gas leaks and vents.

The compensation range for this role is $20-22/hr. Commensurate with experience, skills, and geographic location.

To thrive in this role, you’ll be comfortable taking ownership of the following responsibilities:

Assisting in coordinating and navigating to various facilities with maps and GPS
Helping to calibrate and maintain equipment
Using various detection and measurement technologies under the supervision of the Team Lead
Collecting and recording emission data
Preparing field reports as required

Your Expertise And Skills

These requirements reflect the knowledge, skills and abilities that help you do your best work here.

Experience in Oil and Gas industry (preference given to candidates with natural gas processing/transmission facility experience)
Effective computer skills (Excel and Microsoft Office are essential) and proficiency with Android OS
Ability to work 12-hour shifts (days only)
Valid driver's license
Preference will be given to candidates with an associate or bachelor's degree in engineering technology or applicable technical degree/diploma; related work experience in hydrocarbon detection and measurement, LDAR, instrumentation or stack emission testing or a mechanical background are also preferred, but not required

Work Environment And Physical Requirements

Ability to walk and/or stand while handling/carrying various technical equipment for extended periods of time
Comfortable occasionally working at heights in a safe manner
Ability to lift 50lbs unassisted
Comfortable working outside in all-weather elements
Ability to climb ladders and stairs
Ability to pass pre-employment drug screen and background check

#INDMEG

Our scientists, engineers, field teams and consultants apply systems thinking that unites science, data and practical expertise to deliver solutions that strengthen our clients’ resilience, mitigate risk and protect the air, water and soil that sustain communities, while uncovering responsible paths forward for planet and progress. For more information, visit www.onterris.com.

We acknowledge that these experiences and perspectives help to enrich our teams and contribute to our ongoing success. jobs.title: Project Coordinator (Accounting)
jobs.description:
Caravel
  |  BPM Technology Solutions

Project Coordinator (Accounting)

Delivery Operations / PMO (TSS)  ·  Full-time  ·  Remote — Austin, TX or Southern California (US hours)  ·  Early career

About Caravel

Caravel | BPM Technology Solutions is an award-winning NetSuite and Salesforce partner and part of BPM LLP, a Top-40 accounting and advisory firm. For 20+ years and 1,000+ implementations we've helped businesses across North America put the right technology to work — honestly, and without the usual consulting theater. We're a fully remote team with delivery centers across the US, Canada, India, and the Philippines.

About the role

This is a launchpad role for an early-career accounting grad who likes organization, numbers, and seeing how the work actually gets done. As a Project Coordinator, you'll keep our consulting engagements on track and on-budget — managing schedules, tracking utilization, and supporting the billing and finance side of delivery. You'll sit at the intersection of delivery and finance, work alongside senior consultants, and build the foundation to grow toward a consulting career. You'll be billable to client work within about two months and ramp toward full utilization over your first year.

What you'll do

Keep engagements on track — build and maintain project schedules, track milestones and deliverables, and flag risks before they slip

Track consultant time, resourcing, and utilization across engagements so the delivery picture stays current

Support billing and finance — prepare and review time-and-expense entries, assist with invoicing, and help keep billing accurate and on time

Administer SOWs and change orders, and keep project documentation and status reporting clean and up to date

Coordinate across delivery teams, consultants, and clients on schedules, status, and logistics

Partner with the PMO and finance to improve realization, reduce revenue leakage, and tighten collections (DSO)

What you'll bring

A bachelor's degree in accounting (or a closely related field) — recent graduate or early-career

Strong organization and attention to detail; you keep many moving pieces straight without dropping any

Comfort with numbers and spreadsheets (Excel), and genuine interest in how a services business runs and bills

Clear written and verbal communication — you can chase a status update without chasing people off

Ability to work US business hours, based in Austin, TX or Southern California

A proactive, ownership mindset — you spot what needs doing and get it done

Bonus points

Internship or coursework in accounting, finance, or professional-services operations

Exposure to NetSuite, a PSA/project tool (OpenAir, Kantata/Mavenlink, Smartsheet), or billing/T&E systems

Familiarity with consulting delivery, statements of work, or revenue-recognition basics

Location & schedule

Full-time, remote — based in Austin, TX or Southern California, working core US business hours.

Why Caravel

This role is a launchpad. You'll learn how a leading NetSuite and Salesforce consultancy delivers and bills, work shoulder-to-shoulder with senior consultants, and build a foundation to grow toward a consulting track — inside a firm known for being honest to a fault and doing the work the right way.

Compensation & benefits

$58,000–$74,000 USD base, depending on location (Austin vs. Southern California) and experience, plus a clear path to billable, client-facing work and growth toward a consulting career. Fully remote, with the benefits of a globally distributed team.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

Overview

Prime Healthcare is an award-winning health system headquartered in Ontario, California. Prime Healthcare operates 54 hospitals and has more than 360 outpatient locations in 15 states providing more than 3.0million patient visits annually. It is one of the nation’s leading health systems with over 60,000 employees and physicians. Twenty-one of the Prime Healthcare hospitals are members of the Prime Healthcare Foundation, a 501(c)(3) not-for-profit public charity. Prime Healthcare is actively seeking new members to join our corporate team!

Responsibilities

The Project Coordinator will support the planning, coordination, and execution of operational, financial, revenue cycle, and growth initiatives across Prime Healthcare’s Ambulatory Surgery Center Division.

The position works closely with ASC administrators, corporate departments, physicians, clinical leadership, and external partners to track projects, analyze performance, identify opportunities for improvement, and ensure assigned initiatives are completed timely.

Key responsibilities include supporting billing, coding and collections improvement initiatives; monitoring revenue cycle and operational performance; assisting with implementation of new service lines and physician programs; coordinating cost-reduction and process-improvement projects; preparing analyses and reports; and tracking projects through implementation and completion.

Critical to success in this role is strong follow-through, analytical ability, attention to detail, effective communication, and the ability to coordinate multiple initiatives across different surgery centers and departments.

Qualifications

Required qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, Finance, Accounting, Economics, Public Health, or related field.
Recent graduate or 1–2 years of relevant professional, internship, healthcare, analytical, or project coordination experience.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and other business applications.
Ability to coordinate multiple projects, priorities, and deadlines.
Ability to develop and maintain project plans, trackers, reports, and performance analyses.
Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to work with corporate leadership, ASC administrators, physicians, clinical staff, and vendors.
Demonstrated initiative, accountability, attention to detail, and follow-through.
Ability to travel to Prime Healthcare ambulatory surgery centers 25-40%.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience or coursework in healthcare operations, finance, revenue cycle, business analytics, consulting, or project management.
Familiarity with healthcare billing, coding, collections, denials, accounts receivable, or reimbursement.
Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and experience analyzing operational or financial data.
Interest in healthcare operations, process improvement, business development, and implementation of new clinical service lines.

Pay Transparency

Prime Healthcare offers competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package that provides employees the flexibility to tailor benefits according to their individual needs. Our Total Rewards package includes, but is not limited to, paid time off, a 401K retirement plan, medical, dental, and vision coverage, tuition reimbursement, and many more voluntary benefit options. A reasonable compensation estimate for this role, which includes estimated wages, benefits, and other forms of compensation, is $71,760.00 to $93,080.00 on an annualized basis. The exact starting compensation to be offered will be determined at the time of selecting an applicant for hire, in which a wide range of factors will be considered, including but not limited to, skillset, years of applicable experience, education, credentials and licensure.

jobs.title: Program Coordinator - Women's Center
jobs.description:
About Glide

GLIDE is a nationally recognized center for social justice, dedicated to fighting systemic injustices, creating pathways out of poverty and crisis, and transforming lives. Through its integrated comprehensive services, advocacy initiatives, and inclusive community, GLIDE empowers individuals, families, and children to achieve stability and to thrive. GLIDE is on the forefront of addressing some of society’s most pressing issues, including poverty, housing and homelessness, and racial and social justice. GLIDE’s mission is to create a radically inclusive, just, and loving community mobilized to alleviate suffering and break the cycles of poverty and marginalization

Position Summary

GLIDE’s Women’s Center is seeking a compassionate and organized Program Coordinator to support the delivery of services for individuals who identify as women who are in immediate need of housing, essential needs (e.g., food, clothes, hygiene supplies) health and mental health services, navigation, and case management support, group support, etc. due to homelessness, gender-based violence, and trauma. The Women’s Center will assess client’s needs, provide information and support to overcome barriers, provide early intervention, and case management. The Women’s Center Program Coordinator will assist the Senior Director to plan, coordinate, and implement the Center’s programs and services, provide direct services, and support other general operations of the program, such as facilitate /co-facilitate groups and plan Center events. This individual will collaborate with the director , staff, and community partners to ensure compliance with multiple-funding sources and their requirements.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Develop, coordinate, and maintain relationships and collaborations with GLIDE’s programs, established and new community partners to benefit participants and promote GLIDE’s Women’s Center.
Be responsible for the coordination, creation, maintenance of service and/or staff schedules and business documentation ( e.g. reports, flyers).
Working in collaboration with case managers, develop and document Individualized Service Plans (ISPs) for clients, including data entry and reporting through CRM tools. Be responsible for organizing and managing Women’s Center events, which will involve coordinating all logistical aspects.
Provide data coordination and quality assurance checks to ensure services meet predetermined standards and client satisfaction.
Provide low-threshold advocacy and case management, which includes referral, linkages, and assistance to health, health services, legal aid, and other human services and resources to support the client to reach their goals for improved safety, wellness, and quality of life.
Conduct street and community outreach and attend community events to reach women and to promote the Women’s Center.
Collaborate with Director to assign administrative tasks, referrals, cases, etc. to program staff. Ensure timely referral processing and allocation of new cases to other Women’s Center staff.
Perform triage, intakes, needs assessments, service planning, service coordination, and follow up contacts in person, by email or phone with clients and other providers.
Apply strength-based services that are centered around motivational interviewing, cultural humility, and trauma-informed care.
Plan, organize, and oversee group sessions, activities, workshops, and individual support servies for clients Lead /co-facilitate women educational and empowerment groups virtually and onsite.
Maintain files and database records to track client progress. Prepare reports, success stories and challenges for internal review and reporting to external funders and stakeholders,; Ensure timely and accurate compliance with all reporting requirements.
Adhere to professional boundaries and standards. Understand and follow basis ethics, values, and principles of regulatory practices. Adhere to all laws and requirements regarding HIPPA, confidentiality, child protective services, contractual agreements, etc.
Meet professional obligations through efficient work habits such as collaborating with co-workers, meeting deadlines, honoring schedules, attend and actively participating in staff and individual meeting , community meeting , supervision, case conferences, client conferences and in-service trainings.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in relevant field (e.g., psychology, social work, sociology, criminal justice) preferred; or at least four years of experience providing services (e.g., case management, or coordination of services) to women experiencing homelessness, domestic violence, gender-based violence, and/or have been incarcerated.
Demonstrated understanding of the psycho-social and economic issues that impact women.
Group facilitation experience helpful .
F acilitates collaboration among Women’s Center staff and other GLIDE departments.
Ability to develop processes and operations to support the implantation of new ideas and approaches.
Knowledge of trauma informed approaches in supporting vulnerable women with a range of complex needs, particularly women of color experience houselessness, poverty, and other traumatic experiences.
Has the ability to work effectively across cultures.
Ability to plan, prioritize and organize tasks and meet deadlines, Strong attention to detail, particularly documentation of case files and updating database.
Works well under pressure and manages stress effectively in a demanding and fast paced environment.
Commitment to the mission, values, and philosophy of GLIDE.

Physical Requirements

Reasonable accommodations can be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. 

Ability to work on a computer and see details of objects at close range. 
Ability to hear within normal range, and communicate effectively (in person, telephone or Zoom ). 
Finger dexterity and the ability to use all standard office equipment. 
Sit or stand comfortably; and the ability to navigate throughout office spaces (via elevator or stairs). 

$25 - $30 an hour

This is a fulltime (30 hour/week), Non-Exempt position.

Work Environment

GLIDE’s buildings are located in the Tenderloin neighborhood.  GLIDE maintains an "open door" policy to the community and its clients, who frequently enter and leave the building.

This role is covered by the collective bargaining agreement.

jobs.title: Project Coordinator
jobs.description:
AHSHAY Description:

AHSHAY Center (AHSHAY) is comprised of a small group of people (5-8 total). The center seeks to support youth impacted by significant trauma - with a focus on youth incarceration and youth homelessness – through projects, community partnerships, changes in policy and youth leadership development.

The mission of AHSHAY is to build up the fortifiers of hope and wellness for youth and unbuild the fortifications of youth incarceration and youth homelessness. 
AHSHAY’s values include:  Abundance, Relationships, Joy, Wellness, Equity, Co-Creation, Youth Brilliance and Persistence.

We know, through an expansive amount of research data and lived experience, that youth incarceration is ineffective, inefficient, harmful, counter to our societal values and shares common roots with other harms like youth homelessness.

AHSHAY is strategically positioned to bridge a host of perspectives and expertise by being dually connected to the University of Washington and the Tubman Center for Health & Freedom (Tubman). AHSHAY team members and work structure tends to engage people across a spectrum of ages, lived experiences, avocations and perspectives; all with a focus on the voices of youth most- proximate to impact from incarceration and homelessness.

AHSHAY’s Operations Support Manager Position:

Under Tubman’s fiscal sponsorship, the Project Coordinator role is a position that would be hired under Tubman and deployed to AHSHAY.
The Project Coordinator will work under the day-to-day guidance of a Project Manager to help advance AHSHAY projects. The position reports to AHSHAY’s Director and interfaces with all AHSHAY team members as well as external parties. Specific projects will vary over time and it is possible that some support to more than one project at a time will be needed.

Position Primary Purpose:
Support the successful advancement of AHSHAY projects
The Project Coordinator will work closely with a Project Manager to help assure that projects come fully to fruition. This role will participate in aspects of project ideation, development, launch, process advancement, project conclusion, and after-project engagement. The Project Coordinator will be highly organized, talented in relationship-building, skilled in supporting project gatherings, and an enthusiastic team member. The Project Coordinator will function in a way that aligns with AHSHAY values and will contribute, in general ways, to the continuing growth of the center.

Position Key Roles:

Project Planning: In close partnership with the Project Manager and Project Director/Center Director, coordinate and participate in project planning. This can include initial ideation, scope development, project charter creation, and logistical development, including timelines. The project coordinator may be responsible for some of the note-taking and other document development created in support of project planning. 
Project Recruitment: Under a Project Manager’s guidance, the Project Coordinator will take a primary role in project recruitment. This may involve the direct recruitment of youth, intergenerational participants, partner organizations, contributing contracted parties, and other interested people. The Project Coordinator may work with AHSHAY’s Narrative Strategist to distribute relevant project recruitment content.
Project Process: Under a Project Manager’s and Project Director’s guidance, the Project Coordinator will play a vital role in assuring project steps are successfully accomplished. This may involve actively supporting project launch events, helping organize project steps, supporting project gatherings, providing communications to various project partners, being a point of contact, supporting adjustments to project steps that are identified by the Project Manager, and supporting the development of progress reports. Strong interpersonal skills and relationship-maintaining abilities are pivotal to this work.
Project Completion: In close collaboration with a Project Manager, help assure a project comes to successful completion. This can mean contributing to the creation of reports, communicating with contracted parties to assure deliverables are completed in a timely fashion and engagement with youth and other partners after project completion. Some project completion cycles will also involve planning the next iteration of a project and the project coordinator will play an active role in this.
Support AHSHAY Center: The Project Coordinator may play a role in supporting general AHSHAY functions. This includes being an active participant in AHSHAY team meetings, supporting the Operations Support Manager in general operational aspects of the center, being an ambassador that represents AHSHAY values in external activities, and being a thought-contributor to AHSHAY’s growth plans. A strong understanding of AHSHAY values and approaches is important to being successful in this role.

Team Participation and Other Responsibilities 

Participate in weekly staff meetings, semi-annual team retreats and other organizational development opportunities 
Practice wellness and healthy work habits
Support the wellness of team members 
Alignment with AHSHAY values

Qualifications

Computer Skills with experience maintaining databases and other information repositories
Highly organized approach to work
Strong communication and interpersonal skills 
Strong creative problem-solving skills
Respectful approach to working with the youth we support and engage in, as well as the communities they are part of. 
Excellent written and oral communication skills

Work Environment

Pleasant, engaging and inspiring workspace
Mostly office-based with some ability to work remotely
Workspace promotes relationship-building and maintenance with partners

Compensation

Full Time Position, with benefits as determined by Tubman
Opportunities for continuing education and professional development

There’s no pledge more important than the one we make to look after our environment, and we’re committed to helping you do exactly that.

Join us as we strive to ensure a sustainable future for our communities and the world we live in.

Become part of our global network of skilled engineers, scientists, auditors, planners and environmental specialists, all working together to leave this world better than we found it.

Who are we looking for?

Our Environmental group is looking for an Environmental Scientist
to join their team! As a graduate with this group, you will be engaged with projects that involve wetland delineations/assessments & permitting, endangered species surveys, water quality assessments, and ecological & environmental studies. These projects support ecological risk assessments, site characterization and remedial action projects on contaminated sites.

Be part of the dynamic culture! Our workplace thrives on a hybrid model, combining in-office collaboration and flexibility. Join us in office, three days a week to contribute, connect and excel in our vibrant environment.

Working with an energetic and high performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in:

Wetland delineation
Field surveys for rare, threatened or endangered flora and fauna and their habitats
Ecological assessments to classify and map habitat cover types and plant communities
Surface water quality monitoring and sampling
Sediment sampling
Macroinverterate surveys / sampling
Fish, reptile and amphibian surveys
Managing and evaluating chemical and biological data
Evaluating and understanding environmental regulations
Preparing work plans, reports and other written communications

What you will bring to the Team:

Bachelor’s and/or Master’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Management, Biology, Ecology or related field of study
0-2 years of experience conducting wetland delineations and ecological field studies
Proficiency with managing and evaluating chemical and biological data using spreadsheets or database software
Familiarity with geographic information systems (GIS) applications software
Must be physically able to conduct strenuous field studies under field conditions that coincide with survey requirements
Able and willing to travel to job sites as necessary

As a multicultural organization, we encourage individual achievement and recognize the strength of a diverse workforce. GHD is an equal opportunity employer. We provide equal employment opportunities to all qualified employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, genetic information, national origin, sex (including same sex), sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions, age, disability or handicap, citizenship status, service member status, or any other category protected by federal, state, or local law.

About Us

Take on some of the world’s toughest challenges - with GHD supporting you every step of the way.

We'll give you control over your career, empower you to find innovative solutions and help you create a lasting impact.

See where your commitment could take you with GHD.

Our Pledge to You

At GHD, we don’t just believe in the power of commitment, we live and breathe it every day.

That’s why we pledge to empower our people to make a positive impact. Combining our deep technical expertise with the capabilities of our clients and partners, we respond to some of the most complex challenges facing our planet today.

See where your commitment could take you.

That’s the #PowerOfCommitment

Who We Are

GHD is a global professional services company that leads through engineering, architecture, and construction expertise. We are an employee-owned company with over 11,000 diverse and skilled individuals, across more than 200 offices spanning five continents.

The Power of Commitment is our brand promise. It’s what makes us different. We are bound to our stated vision and determination to address humanity’s most urgent needs: to make water, energy and urbanisation sustainable for generations to come.

Job Description

Johnson, Mirmiran & Thompson is a dynamic, 100% employee-owned consulting firm with more than 2,800 professionals, providing a full range of multidisciplinary engineering, architecture, information technology, and related services to public agencies and private clients throughout the United States. JMT is currently ranked #45 on Engineering News-Record’s list of the Top 500 Design Firms.

Position Summary:
JMT is currently seeking a Surveying Technician I - Rodman/Instrument Operator for their Knoxville, Tennessee Office. The successful candidate will be responsible for assisting the survey party crew chief with completing survey tasks and implementing proper surveying techniques in the field, the set-up and operation of survey equipment to collect data and to provide any needed support for the field survey party. This candidate will also assist boundary, topographic, as-built, and construction staking.

Immigration sponsorship or support (e.g. H1B, F-1 CPT/OPT/STEM OPT) is not available for this position,
except for qualified candidates eligible for the TN visa classification.

Essential Functions And Responsibilities

Set-up the tripod and prism for data collection
Label topographic features from field codes
Perform calculations
Conduct field investigations
Document tasks
Complete data entry
Assist Survey/SUE crew with handling and operation of survey and SUE equipment

Nonessential Functions And Responsibilities

Perform other related duties as assigned

Required Skills

Strong work ethic
Strong communication skills
Ability to navigate difficult terrain
Ability to stand for extended periods of time
Must successfully complete and pass JMT's Motor Vehicle screening
Valid Driver’s License Required
Able to pass Background Check

Required Experience

High school diploma or equivalent

Preferred Experience

Related experience

Working Conditions

Work is performed in the field 95% of the time. Ability to extensively perform bending, kneeling, standing, shoveling, and lifting and carrying objects weighing up to 25 lbs as needed. Work may be conducted outside in heat/cold, wet/humid, and dry/arid conditions.

Work is performed within a general office environment 5% of the time. Office work is generally sedentary in nature but may require occasional standing and walking. Lighting and temperature are adequate and there are no hazardous or unpleasant conditions caused by noise, dust, etc. within the office environment. Work is subject to variable weather conditions including but not limited to extreme heat and cold.

Travel

Travel expectations for field work could include projects in middle Tennessee, as well as away from home requiring overnight stays which could be 4 nights per week as required for distant projects. Three-day weekends would follow. Projects could be located at any of our other office locations.

And more…

jobs.description:
STATE PROFILE SUMMARY:
May supervise, guide and instruct the work assignments of staff or serve as lead/subject matter expert (SME). Studies the composition, structure and other physical aspects of the earth. Examine minerals, underground water, waste disposal, land reclamation or other environmental problems to determine physical and chemical properties to ensure quality standards. Conducts field and lab studies to determine geological properties of assigned location.

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:

Performs job responsibilities with minimal supervision
Serves as job expert or organization resource in assigned areas
Advise construction firms and government agencies on road construction, foundation design and land use and resource management.
Assembles, operates, and maintains field and laboratory testing, measuring and mechanical equipment; collects and prepares and fluid samples for analysis.
Conducts detailed studies of bridge foundations, soil surveys, and retaining walls; prepares related reports.
Evaluate site investigations and remediations system design for petroleum releases from storages tanks and pipeline facilities.
Inspect construction projects to analyze problems, apply geological knowledge and use testing equipment and drilling machinery
Review environmental reports to ensure adherence to state and federal laws and rules
Supervises and plans work of assigned staff

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

The selected candidate must meet the advertised minimum qualifications to include State Entry Qualifications as well as Agency Specific Qualifications.

STATE ENTRY QUALIFICATIONS:

Associates degree in geology, geologic sciences or a related field from an accredited college or university and five (5) years of job-related experience or
One (1) year of experience required at the lower-level Geologist 3 (LSP052) or position equivalent.

AGENCY SPECIFIC QUALIFICATIONS:

Knowledge of soils, foundations and earth sciences.
Knowledge of rock and soil types, properties, geological maps and literature relevant to the State of Georgia.
Experience reading and interpreting specifications, plans, contract documents, construction and testing manuals, and other resources.
Experience composing and preparing specifications, technical reports and general correspondence
Three (3) years of Supervisory experience comparable to a Group Leader, Section or Unit Head in a geological related environment
Knowledge of computer applications necessary to operate engineering-analysis programs.
Ability to perform mathematical calculations related to production and placement of materials, including percentages and formulas
Ability to solve analytical problems by choosing appropriately from a variety of mathematical techniques.
Committed to providing quality customer service

AGENCY PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

Possession of a Geologist in Training or Professional Geologist license.
Experience preparing engineering and geological reports.
Experience previewing consultant proposals and reports.

jobs.description:
Take Your Environmental Career to the Next Level

Kleinfelder, a Forbes' Top Employer for Engineers in North America, is committed to a people-first culture, technical excellence, and creating opportunities where employees can thrive!

Are you ready to be challenged, make a difference, and experience professional growth in your career? Kleinfelder's Environmental team is looking for you! From environmental planning, permitting, remediation, and site characterization to chemical data management and hydrogeology, Kleinfelder offers a variety of services designed to provide technically appropriate and cost-effective solutions. 

Step into Your New Role

We are seeking a Senior Environmental Scientist / Ecologist
to join our EP&P team in our Sewickley, PA office.

Job Responsibilities:

The successful candidate will lead field teams in wetland delineations, prepare technical reports, prepare permitting applications to federal, state, and local entities, manage the environmental task in project schedules, and coordinate with internal and external groups to complete project tasks and goals. This is a client facing role, the candidate will be required to convey project related information to a variety of clients. The work will involve primarily technical writing for permitting, environmental task management, and leading field efforts including wetland delineations, site assessments, environmental inspections, endangered species surveys, habitat assessments, and other studies.

Position Requirements:

7-15 years of consulting experience.
Experience conducting wetland delineations in accordance with the USACE 1987 Wetland Delineation Manual and supporting Regional Supplements.
Excellent technical writing and verbal communication skills.
Comprehensive understanding and experience preparing of Section 404, 10, and 401WQC.
Knowledge of environmental laws and regulations, specifically pertaining to wetlands and listed wildlife species.
Ability to work flexible work schedules and availability to meet priority deadlines outside of normal working hours.
A valid driver's license.

Education & Certifications:

BS in an Environmental, Biological or Ecological Science, or Environmental Policy; Masters in a relevant field of study is a plus.
40-hour USACE wetland training.

Preferred Skills/Experience:

Plant and wildlife identification skills and survey and permitting protocols.
Excellent planning and organizational skills with strong problem-solving abilities and analytical skills.
Experience operating GPS units under ArcGIS or Terrasync programs.
Experience in ArcGIS or AutoCAD.
Ability to conduct work year-round in adverse climate and field conditions.
Ability to prioritize effort and effectively be engaged on multiple projects at one time.
Experience developing and completing Threatened and endangered species surveys, and coordination with the USFWS

Following an offer, candidates will be required to satisfactorily complete employment reference checks, verification of professional licensure and/or educational credentials, a motor vehicle report (MVR), and a comprehensive background check.

jobs.title: Program Coordinator (DOH/PHD#11090)
jobs.description:
Salary

$24.88 - $37.32 Hourly

$51,755 - $77,633 Annually

This position is a Pay Band C6

Posting Details

It is mission critical to the Governor¿s Priorities to reduce health disparities and improve health outcomes by providing access to care and services in support of health equity for New Mexicans.

The Office of Community Health Workers (OCHW) within the New Mexico Department of Health (NMDOH) exists to support the Community Health Workers/Representatives (CHW/R) profession and workforce development by leading strategic partnerships and capacity-building initiatives with organizations employing, training, and mentoring or advocating for Community Health Workers (CHWs) statewide.

This Posting will be used for ongoing recruitment and may close at any time. Applicant lists may be screened more than once.

Why does the job exist?

The position exists through annual legislative appropriations to meet the state mandated statutes: Senate Bill (SB) 58 enacting the Community Health Workers (CHW) Act and NMSA 1978 State-Tribal Collaboration Act.

The Office of Community Health Workers seeks to become a statewide convener for and is charged with workforce development through integration of Community Health Workers/Representatives into New Mexico's health and social service care teams and networks. This charge is key in providing a competent workforce by developing strategic partnerships across New Mexico with organizations employing, training, mentoring, and advocating for Community Health Workers/Representatives to support sustainability and workforce development initiatives for indigenous, rural and underserved, and northern communities within New Mexico.

This position will coordinate, direct, and deliver training, community outreach, and networking opportunities; develop social service and health care networks to support state health equity initiatives; and technical assistance to support state Community Health Worker/Representatives re/certification to individuals, communities, and organizations/providers in northern New Mexico and indigenous communities statewide.

How does it get done?

Key Position Responsibilities:

Responsible for coordinating, facilitating, and marketing Community Health Worker (CHW) state certification in the Southern communities of New Mexico.
Responsible for supporting CHW workforce recruitment efforts and activities during community events and/or via community requests in the Southern communities of New Mexico.
Responsible for identifying, coordinating, facilitating, and delivering content specific trainings for Community Health Workers/Representatives (CHW/Rs) monthly and/or conducting ad hoc presentations on various community issues and public health topics and trends in Southern communities of New Mexico.
Responsible for developing and strengthening new and current social service and health care networks for Community Health Workers (CHWs), including CHW organizations/providers within Southern New Mexico, rural and underserved, including bordering states, cities, and towns.
Responsible for engaging, developing, and fostering collaborative working relationships and networks with Southern communities to align efforts that address social determinants of health, assist in resource allocation to improve health outcomes, and develop technical assistance supports for Southern New Mexican communities, including bordering states.
Responsible for development of workplans for state certification and recruitment activities; professional development and training, community outreach and networking, and technical assistance supports for organizations/providers in the Southern communities of New Mexico.
Responsible for planning and implementation of the statewide Office of Community Health Workers strategic plan components: regulations and workforce development, health and social care integration, organizational data systems and CHW/R engagement, and workforce sustainability; including data collection and reporting plans of indigenous, rural and underserved, and Southern New Mexico communities.

Who are the customers?

Individuals and statewide, rural, frontier, and indigenous communities and regions, Community Health Workers/Representatives, Community Health Workers Affiliate organizations/providers, Federally Qualified Health Centers, Indian Health Service Units, Hospitals/Clinics, Public Health Offices, Community Based Organizations, Public School Systems, Higher Learning Institutions, Managed Care Organizations, and other health care and social service providers and networks.

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate for the CHW Southern Coordinator requires a unique blend of cultural humility, structural knowledge, and operational expertise tailored to the unique landscape of Southern New Mexico.

Southern New Mexico presents a distinct, diverse context: a dynamic blend of historic Hispano and colonias communities, agricultural and border regions, and expanding rural towns. Community Health Workers (CHWs) serve as the primary bridge between these underserved areas and complex healthcare systems. The Southern Coordinator will provide the essential training, technical assistance, and workforce support needed for these CHWs to succeed.

The ideal candidate will possess the following key characteristics:

Expertise in New Mexico's Medicaid and Certification Ecosystem

The financial and regulatory landscape for New Mexico health workers has shifted significantly to allow greater autonomy. The ideal candidate has a firm grasp on Medicaid Reimbursement Pathways. They will be capable of training clinics, community health centers, and community-based organizations on how to utilize New Mexico's Medicaid standing orders. This includes navigating billing procedures so CHWs can successfully bill for services like system navigation, health promotion, and social care coordination without needing a direct clinician order for every visit.

Deep Knowledge of State Certification Standards

The Southern Coordinator will be well-versed in the New Mexico Department of Health Office of Community Health Workers (OCHW) certification process. They will be equipped to help workers accumulate the required Core Competencies and Continuing Education Units (CEUs) for state certification and recertification. When required, they will coordinate directly with the OCHW Training/Certification Team to provide targeted technical assistance across the southern region.

Competence in Rural and Frontier Delivery Models

Southern New Mexico spans vast geographic distances - from border communities and agricultural hubs to isolated desert and mountain areas. Traditional training and communication methods frequently face challenges due to limited broadband coverage or long travel distances. Mastery in deploying customer-centered technology is essential. The coordinator must be proficient in delivering both asynchronous (self-paced) online training and virtual communities of practice (similar to the Project ECHO model), effectively balancing these with vital, trust-building in-person site visits. This position requires frequent regional travel.

A Lived Understanding of Southern NM Geographic & Social Realities

The coordinator will understand the day-to-day realities of frontier and border healthcare, where a CHW's daily responsibilities range from health literacy coaching and chronic disease management to navigating unpaved rural roads, supporting agricultural workers, addressing social drivers of health, and assisting families in isolated colonias.

Ability to Nurture Strong Local, Academic, and Non-Profit Partnerships

The candidate should have a proven track record of building collaborative relationships with regional educational institutions (such as NMSU and community colleges), CHW professional associations, local healthcare systems, Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs), and community-based non-profits across the southern counties.

Linguistic Competency and Cultural Integration

Given the demographic fabric of Southern New Mexico, fluency in English and Spanish (bilingual) is essential to effectively communicate, train, and build strong relationships with Spanish-speaking Community Health Workers, promotores, and the communities they serve.

Minimum Qualification

Associate's Degree and two (2) years of experience program administration or project management in areas related to the purpose of the position. Any combination of education and/or direct experience in this occupation totaling four (4) years may substitute for the required education and experience.

Employment Requirements

Driver's License
Defensive Driving Certificate
Background Investigation

Working Conditions

The working conditions for this position require splitting your time between an urban administrative office and hands-on, field-based community engagements across the state.

When you aren't on the road, your work is anchored at the New Mexico Department of Health (NMDOH) complex off San Mateo and Montgomery in Albuquerque. This is a professional state agency environment housing multiple core bureaus, including the Public Health Division's Population and Community Health teams. You will be operating in a standard office/cubicle setting¿handling data entry, compiling technical assistance modules, participating in regional state team meetings, and coordinating with state Medicaid and certification specialists. The office portion of the job is structured but fast-moving, requiring high digital proficiency to manage correspondence, track data for tribal and rural clinics, and host virtual training sessions or webinars,

The true heart of this role takes place outside the office. Frequent in-state travel in New Mexico means traversing vast, topographically diverse, and geographically isolated terrains to visit rural clinics, isolated community spaces and cultural gathering locales. Expect significant highway and rural driving time. Travel to Southern New Mexico or can easily involve multi-hour trips one-way, sometimes navigating unpaved roads and unpredictable seasonal weather (monsoons in summer, snow/mud in winter). Once you arrive at a site, the environment shifts immediately from formal state administration to community-centric public health. You might be conducting an upskilling workshop in a community center, doing a walk-through with a CHW manager at a Federally Qualified Health Center, or gathering feedback in a rural community room.

Because you are balancing office deadlines with distant site visits, you will need excellent self-management and calendar flexibility. Travel often demands early departures or overnight stays depending on how far into the frontier communities your technical assistance is required.

Culturally, the working condition requires high adaptability. You must be able to switch gears seamlessly¿moving from formal, bureaucratic data-tracking and policy discussions at the Homestead building to a position of deep listening, cultural humility, and peer-level collaboration when stepping into colonias, community gatherings, or historic rural communities.

If you thrive in a role where no two weeks look exactly the same¿where you can balance structured administrative planning in Albuquerque with deep, relationship-building field work across the beautiful landscapes of New Mexico¿this setup provides exactly that balance.

You will experience exposure to visual/video display terminal (VTD) and extensive personal computer and phone usage. The ability to lift up to 40 lbs (usually outreach materials), bending, stooping and reaching (during on-site visits) and handling multiple projects and meet numerous deadlines will be expected.

new_jobs.description:
About Glide

GLIDE is a nationally recognized center for social justice, dedicated to fighting systemic injustices, creating pathways out of poverty and crisis, and transforming lives. Through its integrated comprehensive services, advocacy initiatives, and inclusive community, GLIDE empowers individuals, families, and children to achieve stability and to thrive. GLIDE is on the forefront of addressing some of society’s most pressing issues, including poverty, housing and homelessness, and racial and social justice. GLIDE’s mission is to create a radically inclusive, just, and loving community mobilized to alleviate suffering and break the cycles of poverty and marginalization

Position Summary

GLIDE’s Women’s Center is seeking a compassionate and organized Program Coordinator to support the delivery of services for individuals who identify as women who are in immediate need of housing, essential needs (e.g., food, clothes, hygiene supplies) health and mental health services, navigation, and case management support, group support, etc. due to homelessness, gender-based violence, and trauma. The Women’s Center will assess client’s needs, provide information and support to overcome barriers, provide early intervention, and case management. The Women’s Center Program Coordinator will assist the Senior Director to plan, coordinate, and implement the Center’s programs and services, provide direct services, and support other general operations of the program, such as facilitate /co-facilitate groups and plan Center events. This individual will collaborate with the director , staff, and community partners to ensure compliance with multiple-funding sources and their requirements.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Develop, coordinate, and maintain relationships and collaborations with GLIDE’s programs, established and new community partners to benefit participants and promote GLIDE’s Women’s Center.
Be responsible for the coordination, creation, maintenance of service and/or staff schedules and business documentation ( e.g. reports, flyers).
Working in collaboration with case managers, develop and document Individualized Service Plans (ISPs) for clients, including data entry and reporting through CRM tools. Be responsible for organizing and managing Women’s Center events, which will involve coordinating all logistical aspects.
Provide data coordination and quality assurance checks to ensure services meet predetermined standards and client satisfaction.
Provide low-threshold advocacy and case management, which includes referral, linkages, and assistance to health, health services, legal aid, and other human services and resources to support the client to reach their goals for improved safety, wellness, and quality of life.
Conduct street and community outreach and attend community events to reach women and to promote the Women’s Center.
Collaborate with Director to assign administrative tasks, referrals, cases, etc. to program staff. Ensure timely referral processing and allocation of new cases to other Women’s Center staff.
Perform triage, intakes, needs assessments, service planning, service coordination, and follow up contacts in person, by email or phone with clients and other providers.
Apply strength-based services that are centered around motivational interviewing, cultural humility, and trauma-informed care.
Plan, organize, and oversee group sessions, activities, workshops, and individual support servies for clients Lead /co-facilitate women educational and empowerment groups virtually and onsite.
Maintain files and database records to track client progress. Prepare reports, success stories and challenges for internal review and reporting to external funders and stakeholders,; Ensure timely and accurate compliance with all reporting requirements.
Adhere to professional boundaries and standards. Understand and follow basis ethics, values, and principles of regulatory practices. Adhere to all laws and requirements regarding HIPPA, confidentiality, child protective services, contractual agreements, etc.
Meet professional obligations through efficient work habits such as collaborating with co-workers, meeting deadlines, honoring schedules, attend and actively participating in staff and individual meeting , community meeting , supervision, case conferences, client conferences and in-service trainings.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in relevant field (e.g., psychology, social work, sociology, criminal justice) preferred; or at least four years of experience providing services (e.g., case management, or coordination of services) to women experiencing homelessness, domestic violence, gender-based violence, and/or have been incarcerated.
Demonstrated understanding of the psycho-social and economic issues that impact women.
Group facilitation experience helpful .
F acilitates collaboration among Women’s Center staff and other GLIDE departments.
Ability to develop processes and operations to support the implantation of new ideas and approaches.
Knowledge of trauma informed approaches in supporting vulnerable women with a range of complex needs, particularly women of color experience houselessness, poverty, and other traumatic experiences.
Has the ability to work effectively across cultures.
Ability to plan, prioritize and organize tasks and meet deadlines, Strong attention to detail, particularly documentation of case files and updating database.
Works well under pressure and manages stress effectively in a demanding and fast paced environment.
Commitment to the mission, values, and philosophy of GLIDE.

Physical Requirements

Reasonable accommodations can be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. 

Ability to work on a computer and see details of objects at close range. 
Ability to hear within normal range, and communicate effectively (in person, telephone or Zoom ). 
Finger dexterity and the ability to use all standard office equipment. 
Sit or stand comfortably; and the ability to navigate throughout office spaces (via elevator or stairs). 

$25 - $30 an hour

This is a fulltime (30 hour/week), Non-Exempt position.

GLIDE’s buildings are located in the Tenderloin neighborhood.  GLIDE maintains an "open door" policy to the community and its clients, who frequently enter and leave the building.

AHSHAY Description:

AHSHAY Center (AHSHAY) is comprised of a small group of people (5-8 total). The center seeks to support youth impacted by significant trauma - with a focus on youth incarceration and youth homelessness – through projects, community partnerships, changes in policy and youth leadership development.

The mission of AHSHAY is to build up the fortifiers of hope and wellness for youth and unbuild the fortifications of youth incarceration and youth homelessness. 
AHSHAY’s values include:  Abundance, Relationships, Joy, Wellness, Equity, Co-Creation, Youth Brilliance and Persistence.

We know, through an expansive amount of research data and lived experience, that youth incarceration is ineffective, inefficient, harmful, counter to our societal values and shares common roots with other harms like youth homelessness.

AHSHAY is strategically positioned to bridge a host of perspectives and expertise by being dually connected to the University of Washington and the Tubman Center for Health & Freedom (Tubman). AHSHAY team members and work structure tends to engage people across a spectrum of ages, lived experiences, avocations and perspectives; all with a focus on the voices of youth most- proximate to impact from incarceration and homelessness.

AHSHAY’s Operations Support Manager Position:

Under Tubman’s fiscal sponsorship, the Project Coordinator role is a position that would be hired under Tubman and deployed to AHSHAY.
The Project Coordinator will work under the day-to-day guidance of a Project Manager to help advance AHSHAY projects. The position reports to AHSHAY’s Director and interfaces with all AHSHAY team members as well as external parties. Specific projects will vary over time and it is possible that some support to more than one project at a time will be needed.

Position Primary Purpose:
Support the successful advancement of AHSHAY projects
The Project Coordinator will work closely with a Project Manager to help assure that projects come fully to fruition. This role will participate in aspects of project ideation, development, launch, process advancement, project conclusion, and after-project engagement. The Project Coordinator will be highly organized, talented in relationship-building, skilled in supporting project gatherings, and an enthusiastic team member. The Project Coordinator will function in a way that aligns with AHSHAY values and will contribute, in general ways, to the continuing growth of the center.

Position Key Roles:

Project Planning: In close partnership with the Project Manager and Project Director/Center Director, coordinate and participate in project planning. This can include initial ideation, scope development, project charter creation, and logistical development, including timelines. The project coordinator may be responsible for some of the note-taking and other document development created in support of project planning. 
Project Recruitment: Under a Project Manager’s guidance, the Project Coordinator will take a primary role in project recruitment. This may involve the direct recruitment of youth, intergenerational participants, partner organizations, contributing contracted parties, and other interested people. The Project Coordinator may work with AHSHAY’s Narrative Strategist to distribute relevant project recruitment content.
Project Process: Under a Project Manager’s and Project Director’s guidance, the Project Coordinator will play a vital role in assuring project steps are successfully accomplished. This may involve actively supporting project launch events, helping organize project steps, supporting project gatherings, providing communications to various project partners, being a point of contact, supporting adjustments to project steps that are identified by the Project Manager, and supporting the development of progress reports. Strong interpersonal skills and relationship-maintaining abilities are pivotal to this work.
Project Completion: In close collaboration with a Project Manager, help assure a project comes to successful completion. This can mean contributing to the creation of reports, communicating with contracted parties to assure deliverables are completed in a timely fashion and engagement with youth and other partners after project completion. Some project completion cycles will also involve planning the next iteration of a project and the project coordinator will play an active role in this.
Support AHSHAY Center: The Project Coordinator may play a role in supporting general AHSHAY functions. This includes being an active participant in AHSHAY team meetings, supporting the Operations Support Manager in general operational aspects of the center, being an ambassador that represents AHSHAY values in external activities, and being a thought-contributor to AHSHAY’s growth plans. A strong understanding of AHSHAY values and approaches is important to being successful in this role.

Participate in weekly staff meetings, semi-annual team retreats and other organizational development opportunities 
Practice wellness and healthy work habits
Support the wellness of team members 
Alignment with AHSHAY values

Qualifications

Computer Skills with experience maintaining databases and other information repositories
Highly organized approach to work
Strong communication and interpersonal skills 
Strong creative problem-solving skills
Respectful approach to working with the youth we support and engage in, as well as the communities they are part of.

GIS Specialist

McMillen Inc. is looking for a GIS Specialist
to join our Geospatial Group
. In this role, you’ll support scientific and engineering initiatives through cartography, geospatial analysis, data visualization, and spatial data management. You’ll be expected to independently manage GIS efforts across multiple projects while contributing advanced geospatial solutions to our multidisciplinary team.

Who we are:
McMillen, Inc. designs and builds solutions that shape the future of water resources. As an employee-owned firm, we take pride in every project because we know our work truly matters. Our people thrive on solving complex challenges, pushing boundaries, and refining their craft. We don’t look for the complacent or the comfortable. We support continuous learning, cutting-edge technology, and a balanced work-life environment so our employees can build careers they’re proud of.

Our people integrate engineering, environmental, and construction expertise to deliver practical, results-driven outcomes. Responsibilities:

Develop professional-quality maps and cartographic products using ArcGIS Pro
Manage and organize geospatial datasets for engineering and permitting projects
Perform geospatial analysis to support environmental, engineering, and scientific initiatives
Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to deliver innovative GIS solutions
Maintain GIS databases (including metadata) and ensure data quality and accuracy
Develop surveys for field data collection using Field Maps Designer and Survey123
Opportunities to develop web applications (e.g., ArGIS Experience Builder, ArGIS Dashboards, Leaflet, and others) as time and interest allows

0-5 years of experience applying GIS and spatial analysis in support of engineering, hydrology, or environmental science projects
Bachelor’s degree in in an environmental science field with applied geospatial and GIS component or credential.
Experience with ArcGIS Pro
Experience with ArcGIS Online and ESRI web-based applications
Intermediate experience creating professional cartographic products
Understanding of geospatial analysis concepts, including spatial statistics and the Spatial Analyst toolkit (or equivalent open-source tools)
Knowledge of spatial projections and datums
Experience working with geospatial data, including: ESRI Geodatabases, KML, GeoPackage, JSON, Elevation data (DEM, point clouds, TIN), and Satellite imagery (Sentinel, Landsat), Derived Products (Land Cover/Classification)
Strong curiosity, adaptability, and willingness to learn new software and technologies
Ability to support multiple technical disciplines and projects simultaneously
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across disciplines and convey technical concepts to varied audiences.
Strong organization and data management skills.
Knowledge of QGIS and Google Earth Engine preferred
Knowledge of programming languages such as python, R, SQL, and Arcade (ESRI) preferred
Familiarity with geospatial libraries such as GDAL and GRASS GIS preferred.

new_jobs.description:
Summary

Come join a company that strives for Extraordinary People and Exceptional Performance ! Chenega Services & Federal Solutions, LLC,
a Chenega Professional Services
’ company, is looking for a Scientific Data Analyst 3
to support the Injury Biomechanics and Protection Group (IBP) of the U.S. Army Aeromedical Research Laboratory (USAARL) to provide the scientific, programmatic, and technical support to allow responsive, high quality, and timely mission accomplishment within a flexible and changing environment.

Our company offers employees the opportunity to join a team where there is a robust employee benefits program, management engagement, quality leadership, an atmosphere of teamwork, recognition for performance, and promotion opportunities. We actively strive to channel our highly engaged employee’s knowledge, critical thinking, innovative solutions for our clients.

Responsibilities

Provide scientific analytical services related to data acquisition (e.g., instrumentation, high speed video, medical images, or engineering and medical databases), data management, and data analysis according to approved protocols, policies, and/or plans to ensure quality, accuracy, future use, and reproducibility of data/results.
Acquire, manage, and analyze data (obtained from instrumentation, high speed video, medical images, or engineering and medical databases).
Provide scientific analytical services related to data analysis, data scientific and engineering quality assessment, and data management according to approved protocols, policies, and/or plans to ensure quality, accuracy, future use, and reproducibility of data/results (e.g., by following scientific procedures, recording information, documenting research, and properly storing data.)
Perform analysis on large time series engineering/research data by writing and/or developing algorithms and processing data through COTS and/or custom analysis software.
Use, develop, and evaluate recommendations on Best Practices of data management, file structures, and relational databases.
Develop and update appropriate analysis documentation, and store documents and data in accordance with applicable regulations and procedures.
Ensure that plans and execution of analysis meets all applicable regulations, guidance, and procedures.
Provide scientific analytical services by applying the principles of statistics, numerical methods, signal processing, research, dynamics, kinematic motion analysis, and programming. Such application will require individual research, synthesis of research and mathematical literature, programming in MATLAB, modification and use of previously created MATLAB scripts, creation of batch jobs, data quality assessments, and handling large time series data sets. Additionally, documentation of analysis will be required within developed and modified scripts and codes along with scientific documentation such as papers, reports, and presentations.
Provide understanding of data use and analysis needs to a multi-disciplinary team including engineers, physicians, computer scientists, database developers, data entry clerks, data quality assessors, and other biomedical researchers.
Provide services related to the Injury Biomechanics RDT&E efforts, including the development of draft test plans and protocol documentation from literature reviews along with the collection and preparation of data for analysis and synthesis according to policy and procedures of the USAARL.
Work under the guidance of the Principal Investigator, Team Chief, and Group Leadership, using knowledge and training to plan and accomplish research tasks and goals.
Work within a research team with a small team of junior data analysts to accomplish RDT&E objectives, but work independently with minimal direction to solve analytic and technical problems.
Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

May work variable work hours to meet performance requirements (e.g., proposal and reporting deadlines, collaborations, and lab and field data collections), including occasional night and weekend hours.
Must be able to obtain and maintain a state-issued driver’s license for independent travel to restricted meetings and field-data collection locations.
Experience in numerical methods programming, data acquisition, and use of MATLAB, including MATLAB specialty toolboxes such as work with images, signals, and statistics. 
Obtain and maintain Associate Investigator credentials.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Use strong communication skills and professionalism at all times.
Knowledge of commonly-used and advanced concepts, practices, standards, and procedures within mechanics, dynamics, and mathematics as demonstrated through a degree and coursework in a relevant STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) field from an accredited program and demonstrated through publications. 
Excellent oral and written communication skills

Step into Your New Role

We are seeking a Senior Environmental Scientist / Ecologist
to join our EP&P team in our Sewickley, PA office.

The successful candidate will lead field teams in wetland delineations, prepare technical reports, prepare permitting applications to federal, state, and local entities, manage the environmental task in project schedules, and coordinate with internal and external groups to complete project tasks and goals. A valid driver's license.

40-hour USACE wetland training.

Plant and wildlife identification skills and survey and permitting protocols.
Excellent planning and organizational skills with strong problem-solving abilities and analytical skills.
Experience operating GPS units under ArcGIS or Terrasync programs.
Experience in ArcGIS or AutoCAD.
Ability to conduct work year-round in adverse climate and field conditions.
Ability to prioritize effort and effectively be engaged on multiple projects at one time.
Experience developing and completing Threatened and endangered species surveys, and coordination with the USFWS

Research and develop briefing materials on sustainability topics, including decarbonization and building and fleet electrification

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science or a related field

Minimum of one year of experience working with environmental or sustainability-related data

Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and other data management tools preferred

Familiarity with energy efficiency improvements, water conservation measures, and greenhouse gas emissions inventories

Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, including experience drafting technical reports and presenting findings

Experience working with and managing large, complex datasets

Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative, interdisciplinary team

Strong interpersonal skills with a customer service focus

Ability to take initiative, stay organized, and manage multiple tasks

There’s no pledge more important than the one we make to look after our environment, and we’re committed to helping you do exactly that.

Join us as we strive to ensure a sustainable future for our communities and the world we live in.

Become part of our global network of skilled engineers, scientists, auditors, planners and environmental specialists, all working together to leave this world better than we found it.

Who are we looking for?

Our Environmental group is looking for an Environmental Scientist
to join their team! As a graduate with this group, you will be engaged with projects that involve wetland delineations/assessments & permitting, endangered species surveys, water quality assessments, and ecological & environmental studies. These projects support ecological risk assessments, site characterization and remedial action projects on contaminated sites.

Be part of the dynamic culture! Our workplace thrives on a hybrid model, combining in-office collaboration and flexibility. Join us in office, three days a week to contribute, connect and excel in our vibrant environment.

Working with an energetic and high performing team, this position offers a variety of work and will see you involved in:

Wetland delineation
Field surveys for rare, threatened or endangered flora and fauna and their habitats
Ecological assessments to classify and map habitat cover types and plant communities
Surface water quality monitoring and sampling
Sediment sampling
Macroinverterate surveys / sampling
Fish, reptile and amphibian surveys
Managing and evaluating chemical and biological data
Evaluating and understanding environmental regulations
Preparing work plans, reports and other written communications

What you will bring to the Team:

Bachelor’s and/or Master’s degree in Environmental Science, Environmental Management, Biology, Ecology or related field of study
0-2 years of experience conducting wetland delineations and ecological field studies
Proficiency with managing and evaluating chemical and biological data using spreadsheets or database software
Familiarity with geographic information systems (GIS) applications software
Must be physically able to conduct strenuous field studies under field conditions that coincide with survey requirements
Able and willing to travel to job sites as necessary

See where your commitment could take you.

That’s the #PowerOfCommitment
